item.title: Coldest Night Of The Year Raises Funds To Combat Homelessness
item.description: The volunteers gathered Saturday at the Community Renewal Team’s Windsor Street offices in Hartford as part of the second annual Coldest Night of the Year 2K and 5K walk, an annual fundraiser coordinated by CRT and the Connecticut Coalition to End Homelessness.

item.title: CT Senator Demands Vote On War Powers Resolution Following Iran Strikes
item.description: Enacted in 1973, a war powers resolution, also known as a war powers act, requires Congressional authorization or an emergency created by an attack on the United States, its territories or armed forces before a president can send troops into action abroad. It also limits military action to 60 days without Congressional approval or a declaration of war.

item.title: Proposed Privacy Bill Would Limit Data Sharing From Plate Readers, Flock Cameras
item.description: The American Civil Liberties Union of Connecticut has raised concerns about the cameras, saying they can put residents at risk, especially immigrants, LGBTQ+ people, and those seeking reproductive or gender-affirming care out of state.

item.title: Unions Back Bill To Protect Workers’ Jobs At Labor Committee Hearing
item.description: Worker retention is part of House Bill 5003, an omnibus bill that also includes provisions on protecting healthcare workers assaulted on the job, free tuition at CT State for children of service members, and municipal labor union provisions, among other things in the bill’s 40 sections and 68 pages.

item.title: Lamont Vetoes Earmarks From Controversial Bill Passed Under Emergency Certification
item.description: Senate Bill 298 is a wide-ranging omnibus bill that addresses education, warehouse working conditions, police training, firefighter cancer funds, and more.

item.title: Federal Aid For Lead Cleanup Is Receding. That’s A Problem For Cash-Strapped Cities.
item.description: Congress and the Trump administration have partially rolled back the federal rules and resources for lead cleanups, potentially making it more challenging for cash-strapped cities and towns to undertake sweeping lead remediation programs.

item.title: CT Regulators Allow UI $68M Added Revenue
item.description: The Public Utilities Regulatory Authority ruling sets UI’s electric distribution revenue requirement at about $452.8 million and authorizes a 9.45% return on equity.

item.title: Senate Democrats And City Leaders Push For Increase In CT’s School Aid Formula
item.description: Senate Bill 7 would raise the “foundation grant” in the state’s Education Cost Sharing formula — the per-student baseline used to calculate how much aid flows to every school district — from $11,525 today to $15,500 by 2030, a 35% increase.

item.title: Lamont, UConn Officials Celebrate New Affiliation For Waterbury Hospital
item.description: “UConn Health Waterbury Hospital is open,” said Andrew Agwunobi, CEO of the UConn Health Community Network.
